articles.title: August hottest month ever recorded globally as huge El Nino emerges
articles.description: Europe's climate monitor said Thursday that August was the hottest month ever recorded around the world and warned of worse to come, as an unprecedented El Nino pattern grows stronger. Global temperatures over land and sea soared to all-time highs in August and capped an extreme summer of heatwaves and wildfires that ranked the hottest on record for western Europe and the contiguous United States.

articles.title: Zelensky's plane 'almost hit' by drone en route to Oslo, Norway PM says

But a source in the Ukrainian presidency described the claim that Zelensky was at risk as "exaggerated".

articles.title: Hindu sect BAPS comes under scrutiny in France, US

But for Indians in France who have been trying to raise awareness of far-right Hindu groups, it comes too late. The sect came under scrutiny in the US more than five years ago. Now French public opinion is asking how the group got the green light for a mega temple near Paris and why questions were not raised.

articles.title: Infantino's FIFA re-election bid faces setback as France withdraws support

articles.title: L’économie française en plein décrochage par rapport au reste de l’Europe : croissance faible, inflation et chômage en hausse
articles.description: La croissance ne devrait pas dépasser 0,4 % en 2026, contre 0,7 % prévu, selon l’Insee. Les principaux moteurs de la demande – consommation et investissements – sont à l’arrêt, quand l’inflation et le chômage continuent de grimper. Cette contre-performance contraste avec la reprise des autres grandes économies de la zone euro.

articles.title: Russia tricks 'vulnerable' foreigners to fight in Ukraine war, Amnesty reports
articles.description: Foreign nationals are being tricked into fighting for the Russian army against Ukraine through fake job offers, an Amnesty International report said Thursday, citing interviews with prisoners of war. The average targeted recruit is under 40, living in a poorer country and lured by the "promise of a job", Amnesty's secretary-general said.

articles.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev revendique des frappes contre plusieurs ports russes

articles.title: Brazil Supreme Court chief suspends colleagues' rulings amid election row
articles.description: The chief justice of Brazil's Supreme Court stepped in Wednesday to halt conflicting rulings by two fellow judges as a dispute over alleged links between Justice Alexandre de Moraes and a banker accused of fraud deepened. The clash has spilled into the campaign for next month's presidential election, adding to tensions around the court.

articles.title: Houthis seize key Yemeni Red Sea port, sources say, threatening global energy flows
articles.description: Iran-aligned Houthi militants seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday, military sources said, posing a further threat to global energy supplies. Four Yemeni government military sources said the Houthis had gained further leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern outlet of the Red Sea and one of the world's most important shipping routes, and were launching attacks on the strategic ​islands of Hanish.

articles.title: 25 years on, America seeks to keep 9/11 memories alive
articles.description: A quarter century after the era-defining attacks of September 11, the United States is eager to keep alive the memory of a 2001 trauma that is fading as the proportion of Americans who did not experience it firsthand grows. President Donald Trump will pay his respects at the Pentagon rather than in New York, where the attacks by hijacked passenger planes on the World Trade Center towers claimed the largest number of the 2,977 total victims recorded on that day.

articles.title: French Football Federation withdraws support for Infantino's FIFA election bid
articles.description: France will not support the candidacy of Gianni Infantino, who is running for a new term as FIFA president in March 2027, the French Football Federation announced on Thursday. The FFF is aligning itself with the position of other European federations such as Belgium, Italy, Scotland, Sweden and Wales, who have also publicly withdrawn support for Infantino. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports.

articles.title: Revisited: Consequences of the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage are still being felt
articles.description: It is one of the most spectacular acts of sabotage committed since World War II. On the night of September 26, 2022, three of the four pipes of the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 gas pipelines exploded on the seabed of the Baltic Sea. 465 thousand metric tons of methane were released into the atmosphere. The long-standing and strategic link between Russia and Germany severed for good.
